content:
The **Progress M-14M** (also known as **Progress 46** or **46P** in NASA's catalog) was a Russian unmanned cargo spacecraft that resupplied the **International Space Station (ISS)** in 2012. Here’s a detailed overview of its mission:

---

### **1. Basic Information**
- **Mission Name:** Progress M-14M (No. 414 / 46P)
- **Spacecraft Type:** Progress-M (Modified) cargo spacecraft
- **Operator:** Roscosmos (Russian Federal Space Agency)
- **Manufacturer:** RSC Energia
- **Launch Date:** January 25, 2012, **23:06:40 UTC**
- **Launch Site:** **Baikonur Cosmodrome, Kazakhstan** (Site 1/5 – Gagarin’s Start)
- **Launch Vehicle:** **Soyuz-U rocket** (Serial No. A15000-140)
- **Docking Date:** January 28, 2012, **00:08:50 UTC**
- **Docking Port:** **Pirs module (DC-1)** of the ISS
- **Undocking Date:** April 19, 2012, **11:04 UTC**
- **Deorbit Date:** April 28, 2012
- **Reentry & Burnup:** April 28, 2012, over the Pacific Ocean (controlled deorbit)

---

### **2. Mission Objectives**
The primary purpose of **Progress M-14M** was to deliver:
- **Dry cargo** (food, clothing, equipment, experiments)
- **Propellant** (for ISS orbit adjustments)
- **Water** (for the station’s life support systems)
- **Oxygen** (in compressed tanks)
- **Spare parts & maintenance tools**

It also carried **experiments and supplies** for the **Expedition 30 & 31** crews.

---

### **3. Cargo Details**
The spacecraft carried approximately **2,669 kg (5,884 lbs)** of supplies, including:
- **Dry Cargo:** ~1,300 kg (food, scientific gear, medical supplies, personal items)
- **Propellant (for ISS refueling):** ~850 kg (used for orbital reboosts)
- **Water:** ~420 kg (in Rodnik system tanks)
- **Oxygen & Air:** ~50 kg (in high-pressure tanks)

Some notable items:
- **New Orlan-MK spacesuit** (for Russian EVAs)
- **Biological experiments** (e.g., plants, microbes)
- **Hardware for the Russian segment** (e.g., Zvezda module systems)

---

### **4. Docking & Operations**
- **Rendezvous & Docking:**
  - Used the **Kurs-NA** automated docking system (new generation).
  - Docked to the **Pirs module** (which was later decommissioned in 2021).
  - The docking was **automatic**, but cosmonauts **Oleg Kononenko & Anton Shkaplerov** monitored it from inside the ISS.

- **On-Station Operations:**
  - The **Expedition 30 crew** (including NASA astronaut **Dan Burbank**) unloaded the cargo.
  - The spacecraft remained docked for **82 days**.
  - Performed **orbital reboosts** (using its engines to adjust ISS altitude).

- **Undocking & Deorbit:**
  - Undocked on **April 19, 2012**, to free the Pirs port for **Progress M-15M**.
  - Conducted **engine tests** in autonomous flight before deorbit.
  - **Deorbited on April 28, 2012**, and burned up in Earth’s atmosphere over the **South Pacific Ocean**.

---

### **5. Technical Specifications**
- **Mass:**
  - **Total at launch:** ~7,200 kg
  - **Cargo mass:** ~2,669 kg
- **Dimensions:**
  - **Length:** 7.23 m
  - **Diameter:** 2.72 m (max, at the cargo module)
- **Power:** Solar arrays (provided ~600 W)
- **Propulsion:**
  - **Main Engine (SKD):** ~300 kg thrust (for major maneuvers)
  - **Thrusters (DPO-B):** For attitude control

---

### **6. Significance & Anomalies**
- **First Progress flight in 2012** (following the **Progress M-13M** mission in October 2011).
- **No major issues** reported during launch, docking, or operations.
- Part of a **series of successful resupply missions** after the **Progress M-12M (44P) failure** in August 2011 (which crashed due to a **Soyuz-U rocket malfunction**).
- Demonstrated the reliability of the **Kurs-NA docking system** (an upgraded version of Kurs).

---

### **7. Comparison with Other Progress Missions**
| Feature | Progress M-14M (46P) | Progress M-13M (45P) | Progress M-15M (47P) |
|---------|----------------------|----------------------|----------------------|
| **Launch Date** | Jan 25, 2012 | Oct 30, 2011 | Apr 20, 2012 |
| **Docking Port** | Pirs | Pirs | Pirs |
| **Cargo Mass** | ~2,669 kg | ~2,670 kg | ~2,370 kg |
| **Mission Duration** | 82 days | 93 days | 78 days |
| **Notable Events** | Successful | Delayed due to 44P failure | Fast-rendezvous test (6-hour docking) |

---

### **8. Legacy & Follow-Up Missions**
- **Progress M-15M (47P)** followed in **April 2012**, testing a **6-hour fast-rendezvous profile** (later standard for Soyuz & Progress).
- The **Progress-M series** continued until **2015**, when it was replaced by the **Progress-MS** (modernized version).
- **Pirs module** (docking port) was later **decommissioned in 2021** and replaced by the **Nauka module**.

---
---
### **9. Interesting Facts**
- The **Soyuz-U rocket** used for this launch was one of the last of its kind (phased out in 2017).
- **Progress spacecraft** are based on the **Soyuz design** but with a cargo module instead of a crew capsule.
- The **Rodnik water system** (used in Progress) allows for efficient water transfer to the ISS.
- This was the **46th Progress mission to the ISS** since the first one in 2000 (**Progress M1-3**).

---
---
### **10. Sources & Further Reading**
- **NASA ISS Expedition 30/31 Updates** ([NASA.gov](https://www.nasa.gov))
- **Roscosmos Press Releases** ([Roscosmos.ru](https://www.roscosmos.ru))
- **Spaceflight101** ([Spaceflight101.com](https://www.spaceflight101.com))
- **Wikipedia: Progress M-14M** ([Link](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progress_M-14M))
- **Gunter’s Space Page** ([Space.skyrocket.de](https://space.skyrocket.de))
